skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Use when the user asks to review a branch, pull request, or work-in-progress diff against a fixed point. Not for fixing the findings, approving the change, or merging it. Reviews two axes in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side — Standards (this repository's documented coding standards) and Spec (the originating issue or spec).
skills.trigger: the user asks to review a branch, pull request, or work-in-progress diff against a fixed point
skills.nontrigger: fixing the findings, approving the change, or merging it

boundaries.Secrets: Read only tracked review content; never open `.env` files, credential stores, or provider tokens, and never copy secret-shaped strings into a finding.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Never reset, stash, stage, or overwrite unrelated working-tree changes; inspect staged, unstaged, and untracked surfaces without modifying them.
boundaries.Migration: Do not apply, revert, or generate database migrations; a migration-file change in the diff is reported as a finding only.
boundaries.Generated files: Treat generated artifacts as review inputs and never regenerate them; report drift between a generator and its committed output instead.
boundaries.Provider: Make no provider calls; issue-tracker retrieval is the only external read, and its authentication state is reported when unavailable.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and report when the fixed point does not resolve, when no requested review surface is non-empty, or when the originating spec cannot be located; a stopped axis is reported as skipped, never as a pass.
skills.cleanup: none — the review leaves no files, comments, issues, or PR artifacts behind.

skills.name: code-simplification
skills.description: Use when existing code works but is hard to read, maintain, or extend and behavior must not change. Not for behavior changes, for code whose intent is not yet understood, or for performance-critical paths. Simplifies code for clarity while preserving behavior exactly.
skills.trigger: existing code works but is hard to read, maintain, or extend and behavior must not change
skills.nontrigger: behavior changes, for code whose intent is not yet understood, or for performance-critical paths

boundaries.Secrets: Never inline secret values, and never refactor credential-bearing configuration into code; secret material stays where it is.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Preserve pre-existing and unrelated working-tree edits; confine refactors to the requested scope and report anything left out.
boundaries.Migration: Do not edit migration files or schema history; a simplification that would require a migration is out of scope.
boundaries.Generated files: Never hand-edit generated output; simplify the generator or the source it reads instead.
boundaries.Provider: Make no provider calls; the pass is local analysis over the supplied code region.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and revert the increment when a test, type check, or lint run fails, when the intent of the code is not yet understood, or when the change would alter a public API surface.
skills.cleanup: no dead code, unused imports, or unreachable branches left behind by the pass; speculative abstractions removed are gone, not commented out.

skills.name: control-plane-audit
skills.description: Use when the user asks for a repository-wide milestone acceptance or production-readiness audit across the managed-cloud, Local, and self-hosted profiles. Not for an ordinary isolated bug fix or a single-file change. Routes to the smallest relevant evidence lane and never infers qualification from closed issues or green CI.
skills.trigger: the user asks for a repository-wide milestone acceptance or production-readiness audit across the managed-cloud, Local, and self-hosted profiles
skills.nontrigger: an ordinary isolated bug fix or a single-file change

boundaries.Secrets: Never read credential values, tokens, or secret stores to satisfy an audit lane; name the secret-protected evidence that is missing instead of retrieving it.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Record the candidate's dirty state and never clean, reset, stash, or commit anything during an audit request.
boundaries.Migration: Migration and restore evidence is reproduced only under the selected profile; an unapplied migration is never reported as applied.
boundaries.Generated files: Regenerate nothing; when a generated artifact drifts from its source, report the drift and its generator instead of editing the artifact.
boundaries.Provider: No provider activation and no paid calls; provider-dependent lanes stay explicitly blocked with their activation prerequisites named.

skills.stopConditions: Stop the affected lane and report when the authoritative issue criteria or candidate identity cannot be established, when the environment or credential for a live profile is unavailable, or when a required lane was skipped; unaffected lanes continue.
skills.cleanup: include task-owned resource cleanup in the handoff and list intentionally retained resources.

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.description: Use when a change spans more than one file or is too large to land in one step. Not for a single-file, single-function change of minimal scope. Delivers multi-file changes as thin vertical slices — implement, test, verify, and checkpoint each increment.
skills.trigger: a change spans more than one file or is too large to land in one step
skills.nontrigger: a single-file, single-function change of minimal scope

boundaries.Secrets: Never commit, log, or print credentials while staging increments; secret material stays in its configured store.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Inspect the starting worktree, preserve pre-existing and unrelated user changes, and never stage or clean them.
boundaries.Migration: A migration is its own increment with its own verification; an increment that changes schema is not complete until the migration check passes.
boundaries.Generated files: Regenerate committed generated files with their pinned generator inside the same increment as the source change that produced them.
boundaries.Provider: No provider activation and no deployment; a provider-dependent increment stays blocked with its prerequisite named.

skills.stopConditions: Stop the cycle when an increment fails verification, when the requested scope is unclear, or when the next slice would need a decision reserved for the user.
skills.cleanup: remove or document task-owned scaffolding, fixtures, and temporary files; preserve pre-existing and unrelated user changes, and report them rather than staging or cleaning them.

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.description: Use when the code handles untrusted input, authentication, data storage, external integrations, or personal data. Not for pure configuration, documentation, or static content with no security surface. Threat-models first, then hardens against OWASP patterns, SSRF, supply chain, privacy, and the LLM attack surface.
skills.trigger: the code handles untrusted input, authentication, data storage, external integrations, or personal data
skills.nontrigger: pure configuration, documentation, or static content with no security surface

boundaries.Secrets: Never read, print, log, or commit real secrets; use synthetic canaries, and treat a committed secret as a rotation event rather than a deletion.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Hardening edits stay inside the reviewed scope and never reset, stash, or overwrite unrelated working-tree changes.
boundaries.Migration: A schema or migration change that weakens a security control requires explicit approval and its own regression test.
boundaries.Generated files: Do not hand-patch generated clients or schemas; apply the control to the generator or the committed source instead.
boundaries.Provider: No provider credential changes and no provider activation; provider trust findings are reported with their activation prerequisite.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and request approval before an "Ask First" item, before weakening an existing control, and before any change to credentials, roles, or external access.
skills.cleanup: no secrets, PII, or test credentials left in code, fixtures, logs, or git history; a committed secret triggers rotation, not just deletion.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Use when implementing logic, fixing a bug, or changing any existing behavior. Not for pure configuration, documentation, or static content that has no observable behavior to test. Drives the change with RED to GREEN to REFACTOR discipline and a prove-it reproduction test for every bug fix.
skills.trigger: implementing logic, fixing a bug, or changing any existing behavior
skills.nontrigger: pure configuration, documentation, or static content that has no observable behavior to test

boundaries.Secrets: Fixtures use synthetic values only; a test never embeds a real credential and never reads one from a live store.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Test runs and fixture edits never reset, stash, or overwrite unrelated working-tree changes.
boundaries.Migration: A behavior change that needs a migration ships the migration and its test in the same change; a green suite alone does not prove the schema.
boundaries.Generated files: Snapshots and generated fixtures are regenerated by their generator and never hand-edited to make a test pass.
boundaries.Provider: Tests run against local fakes or approved offline fixtures; no provider call is required to prove a behavior change.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and report when the RED test cannot be made to fail for the right reason, when the suite was already red before the change, or when the only route to green is to skip, stub, or delete a test.
skills.cleanup: no skipped, stubbed, or disabled tests left behind; test state stays isolated, deterministic, and free of secrets.

skills.name: turborepo
skills.description: Use when the question is about turbo.json, task pipelines, dependsOn, caching, the turbo CLI, --filter or --affected, CI optimization, or monorepo package boundaries. Not for general package-manager, application-framework, or non-Turborepo build questions. Covers task graphs, caching, filtering, environment variables, and package boundaries.
skills.trigger: the question is about turbo.json, task pipelines, dependsOn, caching, the turbo CLI, --filter or --affected, CI optimization, or monorepo package boundaries
skills.nontrigger: general package-manager, application-framework, or non-Turborepo build questions

boundaries.Secrets: Never inline environment secrets into task definitions or cached outputs; variables stay in the environment configuration.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Task-graph changes never reset, stash, or discard working-tree edits; the pipeline is verified against the current tree.
boundaries.Migration: Migrations are separate tasks with their own dependsOn edges; a task must never imply that a migration ran.
boundaries.Generated files: Generated outputs are produced by the declared pipeline task rather than committed by hand.
boundaries.Provider: No provider activation is implied by a task graph; tasks that call providers stay explicit and separately authorized.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and report when a task's declared output would change, when the dependency graph cannot express the required ordering, or when a cache configuration would hide a failing task.
skills.cleanup: no root-package task logic, `&&`-chained scripts, or leftover `prebuild` shims remain; reverted experiments leave no orphan config keys.

provenance.source: Vercel Turborepo agent skill (upstream docs: apps/docs/content/docs/ in the Turborepo repository, https://turborepo.dev/docs)

skills.name: typescript-advanced-types
skills.description: Use when designing complex TypeScript type logic such as generics, conditional types, mapped types, template literals, or reusable utility types. Not for everyday typing that the compiler already infers correctly. Reference for type-level design and compile-time type safety.
skills.trigger: designing complex TypeScript type logic such as generics, conditional types, mapped types, template literals, or reusable utility types
skills.nontrigger: everyday typing that the compiler already infers correctly

boundaries.Secrets: Type definitions never encode real credentials or personal data; use an opaque placeholder type for sensitive values.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Type-only edits stay inside the requested scope and never reset or overwrite unrelated working-tree changes.
boundaries.Migration: A type change that alters persisted or API types requires the matching schema or migration change in the same change.
boundaries.Generated files: Never hand-edit generated declaration or schema files; change the source type and regenerate.
boundaries.Provider: Make no provider calls; type-level verification is local compilation.

skills.stopConditions: Stop and report when the type change cannot be expressed under strict mode without an `any` escape, when the compiler errors are pre-existing, or when a type-level test passes when it should fail.
skills.cleanup: no temporary `any`, `as unknown as`, or experimental type aliases left in the diff.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Use when about to claim that work is complete, fixed, or passing, including before a commit or pull request. Not for performing the work itself or for restating a status that was never verified. Requires running the verification command and reading its output before making any success claim.
skills.trigger: about to claim that work is complete, fixed, or passing, including before a commit or pull request
skills.nontrigger: performing the work itself or for restating a status that was never verified

boundaries.Secrets: Verification output is reported without secret values; a command that would print credentials is not run and is reported as skipped.
boundaries.Dirty worktree: Verification is read-only over the working tree; it never cleans, resets, stages, or commits changes.
boundaries.Migration: A migration claim requires the migration check to have run; an unrun migration check leaves the claim unverified.
boundaries.Generated files: Generated artifacts are verified by their generator or drift check, never by asserting that the committed file looks right.
boundaries.Provider: No provider activation and no paid call is implied by verification; a provider-dependent check stays unverified and is named as such.

skills.stopConditions: Stop the claim when any required command fails, when a required command cannot run, or when the observed output does not match the claim being made.
skills.cleanup: none — verification leaves no artifacts; it records only the commands run and their results.
